product: Portfolio of habit-tracking, focus-timer, and journaling apps (HabitKit flagship)
why_worked: Quit enterprise C#/.NET job, gave himself a 12-month runway, went deep on ONE platform (native SwiftUI) and ONE proven category (habit tracking), Top-5 US App Store ranking in category drove organic ASO growth at $1-2/mo micro-subscription price point across 25K+ payers.
failure_modes: Initially built in Flutter — switched to native SwiftUI after concluding cross-platform cost native-feel and App Store ranking signal
Single-category focus took 12mo of committed runway before payoff, not a fast win

product: Portfolio of 28 small mobile/web micro-apps (utilities, browser extensions, micro-SaaS) shipped serially over 8 months while working full-time
mrr_or_arr: $100 MRR -> $25K MRR by Dec 2025 ($84K cumulative revenue)
why_worked: Abandoned single-perfect-app strategy (had burned months polishing apps that never launched) in favor of ship-fast-let-data-decide portfolio approach; AI coding tools (Claude, Cursor, Lovable) compressed build time 50-70% letting one person maintain 28 concurrent small products and kill losers fast.
failure_modes: Most of the 28 apps individually made near-zero revenue — portfolio power law, not per-app reliability
Still full-time employed in parallel, meaning real hours/week invested were compressed and exhausting

product: 143 shipped apps across categories; 11 apps crossed $100/mo, best single app ~$1,870/mo
tech_stack: not fully disclosed — solo-dev rapid-ship toolchain, cross-platform
mrr_or_arr: ~$4.8K MRR total across portfolio (up from $2.1K prior month)
why_worked: Extreme volume/iteration strategy — treat each app as a lottery ticket, most fail, a small number carry the portfolio; explicit admission marketing (not building) is still the hard/gambling part even after 143 launches.
failure_modes: 132 of 143 apps generate negligible or zero revenue
Founder's own framing: 'marketing still feels like gambling' after years of practice — discovery/ASO is not a solved problem even at high volume

product: Wunderfind — Find Lost Device (AirPods/Bluetooth headphone finder utility)
why_worked: Solved one narrow, high-frequency pain (lost AirPods) with a single-purpose utility; no-ads subscription model plus strong ASO from a huge organic rating base; eventually listed for acquisition at $400K, showing utility apps compound into sellable assets.
failure_modes: Extremely narrow niche — success is hard to replicate outside a hardware-attach pain point (AirPods ubiquity did the marketing)
Two-person team needed for iOS+Android parity, not a true solo case

product: AI-powered professional headshot generator, proprietary pipeline layered on Stable Diffusion + DreamBooth stacking dozens of models for 10x output quality
why_worked: Web-first AI-vision product (not app-store gated), organic search/content drove $300K+ revenue without paid ads; prior exit (Headlime, acquired by Jasper in 8 months) gave him distribution credibility and reusable playbook; technical differentiation (model stacking) beat single-model competitors on perceived quality, justifying premium one-time pricing.
failure_modes: Not an app-store case at all — distribution was web/SEO, so App Store ASO lessons don't transfer directly
Category (AI headshots) got crowded fast post-2023 as the underlying models became commodity APIs

tech_stack: not fully disclosed — mobile-native, RevenueCat-style subscription billing implied by category norm
why_worked: Consistent, unglamorous 8-month grind in a proven category (habit tracking) with public build-in-progress posts on Indie Hackers driving a trickle of organic signups.
failure_modes: 8 months is the FLOOR to reach just $1K MRR in a crowded, low-differentiation category — slow floor case, not a fast win
No stated differentiation beyond execution consistency, meaning the result is closer to typical/base-rate than exceptional
